analysis: The only change in this PR is one added documentation row at docs/reference/configuration.md:414. It describes DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED, an environment switch that selects the Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models. The row says the variable is read once per process, is not forwarded to LaunchAgents, and that forced kernels (`packed`/`rows`) skip the bit-for-bit parity check and are for A/B measurement only. The PR contains no source changes, so no code path, authentication, encryption, attestation, key custody, cache storage or authorization behavior is altered. I considered whether the variable creates a security regression against TB-007 (provider inference engine) or TB-003 (operator versus process), and concluded it does not. Anyone who can set the environment of the provider process already has operator-level control, which TB-003 already treats as adversarial and covers through the attestation, hardened runtime and EnvironmentScrubber controls. The variable is not on the LaunchAgent allow-list, so installed daemons keep the default probe, and the default probe keeps a four-row kernel only where it matches the stock kernel bit for bit. A malicious provider could already serve manipulated outputs (T-007), and a forced kernel adds no capability beyond that. The kernel choice does not touch prefix-cache storage or the lookup-tag, TTL and salt controls in T-041. Remaining unverified contract: the referenced implementation in libs/mlx-swift-lm GatedDelta.swift and the docs/architecture/inference.md anchor were not supplied, so I cannot confirm the documented behavior matches the code. This affects documentation accuracy only, not a demonstrated security conclusion.
